properties.name: A discipline that applies mid-task is delivered at the tool that triggers it, not from a catalogue read once at handshake
properties.statement:
SKILLS SPLIT INTO TWO KINDS AND THEY NEED DIFFERENT DELIVERY. A **task-skill** (genesis, adopt, capture-intent, governance-proposal, plan-increments) is reached for at a recognisable task boundary — the agent is STARTING something and asks what covers it. A **discipline-skill** (revise-design's snapshot-first, capture-intent's search-before-you-create, link-artifacts' hash-after) applies at an arbitrary instant INSIDE another task, when the agent is mid-flow and not asking anything.

THE CATALOGUE SERVES THE FIRST AND STRUCTURALLY CANNOT SERVE THE SECOND. `dec:skills-served` put the skill catalogue into the server instructions, which every client injects at handshake — deliberately, as "progressive disclosure rebuilt by hand", and it is the price of never being stale. It works: an agent that has read the catalogue reaches for the right task-skill. But a catalogue is read ONCE, and a discipline applies thousands of tokens later at a moment nothing announces. **The delivery mechanism and the trigger moment are mismatched, and no amount of restating the catalogue closes that gap.**

⭐ MEASURED ON THIS SESSION, which is the evidence rather than the theory (2026-08-09, `fact:which-skills-a-session-reached-for-and-why`): every skill used unprompted followed a task boundary the user had just created. Every skill MISSED was a discipline applying incidentally inside other work — two revisions made without loading revise-design, and two Contributors minted without the namespace search capture-intent prescribes. The snapshot discipline was followed ONLY because a consumer's report quoting it happened to be open in context. That is a near miss, not self-direction.

THE MECHANISM THAT ALREADY WORKS AND IS NOT APPLIED HERE: `loop_hint` rides on tool RESPONSES — `add_requirement` returns "when this capture batch lands, run detect_gaps" — and it demonstrably changes behaviour, because it arrives at the moment of the action rather than at the start of the session. The same carrier should name the discipline: a revising `create_node` saying "this is a revision; revise-design takes the snapshot FIRST, and after the edit it cannot be recreated"; `delete_node` / `delete_edge` likewise. This is `rule:bl-135`'s guardrail principle — state the FAILURE MODE, not the rule — applied to routing rather than to warnings, and that principle carries a blind trial behind it: an agent complied with those docstrings without knowing they were interventions.

⭐⭐ AND THE STRONGER FORM, WHICH DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE AGENT AT ALL. `dec:loop-status-state-not-history` holds that loop debt is computed from GRAPH STATE, never from run history. Apply the same rule to discipline: do not track whether a skill was INVOKED — compute whether its OUTCOME IS PRESENT. A node revised with no Snapshot at the current epoch is detectable from graph state alone, and that survives an agent which ignores every hint. dragon Boss (dev_storyflow) proposed the identical shape independently: "have delete_edge / a revising create_node report whether the target has a snapshot at the current epoch — NOT BLOCK, JUST SAY."

⚠️ THE ASYMMETRY THAT LIMITS THIS, stated so the requirement is not read as covering more than it can: a revision with no snapshot IS computable; a node created without a prior search is NOT — nothing distinguishes it from a node created after a search that found nothing. So discipline-skills split a second time. Those whose neglect leaves evidence get a detector; the rest can only ever get a hint, and a hint is what they get.

WHAT THIS MUST NOT BECOME: a blocking gate. A tool that blocks becomes a tool people route around, and then the graph stops matching reality — the one failure it cannot survive. And not another restatement in AGENTS.md: four skill-versus-tool drifts are already on record, and `req:a-rule-knows-where-else-it-is-written-down` exists because restatements rot.

RAISED BY ANTHONY, 2026-08-09: "continue to think how do we continue to improve the probability that an agent will use reflow2's skills and tools without being reminded."
